title.narrative: Spotlight Initiative 2.0 Sierra Leone (Direct Coordination Costs)

description.narrative: The Spotlight Initiative 2.0 Programme in Sierra Leone employs a holistic, multisectoral strategy to address the critical barriers to eliminating violence against women and girls (VAWG) and harmful practices. The programme seeks to strengthen the legal and institutional framework to address important gaps and discrepancies in legal content and implementation, particularly regarding the prevention of female genital mutilation (FGM) and harmful traditional practices (HTP). Alongside the Ministry of Gender, the programme supports the national rollout of the GBV Information Management System (GBVIMS) to enhance data-driven and evidence-based policymaking and programming. The Spotlight Initiative in Sierra Leone builds on existing frameworks and adopts experimental and integrated approaches to reshape societal norms, attitudes and behaviours at individual, family and community levels. Activities include school-related interventions to promote gender equality and reduce violence, leadership initiatives, community-led dialogues to co-create solutions with community and traditional leaders, CSOs, women’s groups, men and boys.Additionally, the Programme strengthens and expands survivor-centred response services, including access to justice, healthcare, and psychosocial support, ensuring accessibility, high quality of services and sustainability of impact achieved. The comprehensive approach works to strengthen infrastructure, data systems, build capacities of government-led service providers and community outreach to create a responsive and sustainable framework that can adapt to local contexts, respond effectively to population needs and scale. By anchoring activities within national frameworks, the programme seeks to strengthen government ownership and accountability, fostering long-term resilience in quality service provision.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
